Founders Day Stories, 1940–1964

1940California Eagle · Los Angeles, California

Hattie McDaniel and Sigma Gamma Rho

YMCA Schedule Subscription Banquet · Thursday, November 7, 1940 · Page 4

“Soror Hattie McDaniel, winner of the Motion Picture Academy award and charter member of Sigma Gamma Rho sorority, will give several brilliant numbers.”

The Los Angeles YMCA held its first annual subscription banquet on November 14, one week after this notice appeared. Mary Lou Gardner, one of the sorority’s founders, gave the welcome. Hattie McDaniel, a charter member of the Los Angeles chapter, was also on the program that evening.

1950Arizona Sun · Phoenix, Arizona

Founders Day To Be Observed

Beta Mu Sigma at First Institutional Baptist Church · Thursday, November 16, 1950 · Page 4

“The Beta Mu Sigmas of the Sigma Gamma Rho Sorority chapter will observe Founders Day with an appropriate program Sunday evening, November 12 at 3 p.m. at the First Institutional Baptist Church, 517 East Jefferson Street.”

The program took place on Founders Day itself, Sunday, November 12. Beta Mu Sigma hosted at First Institutional Baptist Church. Soror Crosland traveled from Los Angeles to give the address. Local chapters were invited, along with friends and the general public.

1954The Oregon Daily Journal · Portland, Oregon

Sorority Plans Special Events

Beta Eta Sigma’s Founders’ Day anniversary · Thursday, November 11, 1954 · Page 44

“Beta Eta Sigma chapter of Sigma Gamma Rho sorority will celebrate its Founders’ day anniversary, Sunday, November 14, by worshipping in a group at the 11 o’clock service at Hughes Memorial church.”

The chapter worshipped together at the 11 o’clock service at Hughes Memorial Church. That afternoon, from 2 to 6 p.m., the chapter held its annual Founders’ Day tea at the home of Mrs. Wilber Marshall on NE Thompson Street.

1958Oakland Tribune · Oakland, California

Race Relations Lecture Topic

A public lecture by Sally N. Edwards · Tuesday, November 11, 1958 · Page 11

“Sally N. Edwards … is a former president of Sigma Gamma Rho sorority, and has served on the executive board of the National Council of Negro Women.”

The Arlington Women’s Club scheduled a world affairs lecture on race relations for 1 p.m. the next day at Arlington Community Church, and Sally N. Edwards of the San Francisco YWCA was the speaker. This clipping is not from a Founders Day program. It records a soror speaking in public on race relations in 1958.

1964The Berkeley Gazette · Berkeley, California

Sigma Gammas’ Founders Week

A full week of worship, rededication, and service · Saturday, November 14, 1964 · Page 8

“Morning worship services at Oakland’s Morning Star Church began Sigma Gamma Rho’s Founders Week observance in the Bay Area … Founded in 1922 and dedicated to progress and service.”

Morning worship at Oakland’s Morning Star Church opened the week. Members of Beta Theta Sigma then gathered for a Rededication Hour at the home of Mrs. Ann Stedman, where national officer Lillie Wilkes led the meditation. The article also mentions the chapter’s yearly scholarship for a student and its help for people in need.
